questions.context: I took my laptop to the repair shop, but a technician was on holiday.
questions.instruction: Rewrite the sentence with the error corrected.
questions.correctAnswer: I took my laptop to the repair shop, but the technician was on holiday.
questions.explanation: The technician is a specific person the listener can identify from the shop, so 'the' fits better than 'a'.

commonWrongAnswers.answer: I took my laptop to the repair shop, but technician was on holiday.
commonWrongAnswers.comment: You can't leave out the article here, because 'technician' is a singular countable noun and needs one.

commonWrongAnswers.answer: I took my laptop to repair shop, but a technician was on holiday.
commonWrongAnswers.comment: You changed the wrong part; 'the repair shop' is fine, and the error is elsewhere.

questions.context: My phone battery is almost dead, so I must to charge it now.
questions.instruction: Rewrite the sentence with the error corrected.
questions.correctAnswer: My phone battery is almost dead, so I must charge it now.
questions.explanation: Modal verbs like 'must' are followed by the base verb without 'to', so it's 'must charge'.

commonWrongAnswers.answer: My phone battery is almost dead, so I must charging it now.
commonWrongAnswers.comment: After a modal verb you use the plain base form, not the -ing form.

commonWrongAnswers.answer: My phone battery is almost dead, so I musts charge it now.
commonWrongAnswers.comment: Modal verbs never take -s, even after 'I' or 'he'; and the extra 'to' is the real problem.

questions.context: Yesterday my brother said, "I will send you the app link tonight." Later he told me that he ___ send me the app link that night.
questions.instruction: Fill in the blank with one word.
questions.explanation: In reported speech after a past verb like 'told', 'will' usually changes to 'would'.

commonWrongAnswers.comment: It's tempting to keep the original word, but after 'told' in the past, 'will' usually shifts back.
'Can' changes the meaning to ability; the original promise was with 'will', which becomes 'would'.
'Should' means advice or obligation, which isn't what the promise expressed.

questions.context: She suggested to use a different app for the video call.
questions.instruction: Rewrite the sentence with the error corrected.
questions.correctAnswer: She suggested using a different app for the video call.
questions.explanation: After 'suggest', the next verb takes -ing, so it's 'suggested using'.

commonWrongAnswers.answer: She suggested to using a different app for the video call.
commonWrongAnswers.comment: You added -ing but kept 'to'; 'suggest' is followed directly by the -ing form.

commonWrongAnswers.answer: She suggested use a different app for the video call.
commonWrongAnswers.comment: The base form doesn't work after 'suggest' here; you need the -ing form.

questions.context: My computer is very slow today. It ___ the software update since 9 a.m., and it still hasn't finished.
questions.instruction: Fill in the blank with the correct form of 'install'.
questions.explanation: The action started at 9 a.m. and is still going now, so the present perfect continuous fits.

commonWrongAnswers.comment: 'Since 9 a.m.' links the past to now, so the present continuous alone doesn't work.
The simple past suggests it's finished, but the update is still going.
This suggests the installation is complete, but the sentence says it hasn't finished.
